question.problem:
In a particular shop, eggs are sold in cartons. There are $10$ eggs in each carton. The weight of an egg, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $60\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $5\,\text{g},$ while the weight of a carton, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $30\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\text{g}.$ If one carton containing eggs is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs less than $653\,\text{g}?$ You may assume that the weights are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8849\,$ | $\,0.8869\,$ | $\,0.8888\,$ | $\,0.8907\,$ | $\,0.8925\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9032\,$ | $\,0.9049\,$ | $\,0.9066\,$ | $\,0.9082\,$ | $\,0.9099\,$ |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9192\,$ | $\,0.9207\,$ | $\,0.9222\,$ | $\,0.9236\,$ | $\,0.9251\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the weight of an $i$th egg, and let $Y$ denote the weight of a carton. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(60,{5}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 10,
$$

and

$$
Y∼N(30,{2}^{2}).
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the weight of a randomly selected carton with eggs. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{10}+Y,
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =10\cdot 60+30 \\  & =630, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =10\cdot {5}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\  & =254.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(630,254).
$$

In order to find $P(W<653),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W<653) & =P(Z<\frac{653-630}{\sqrt{254}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<1.44) \\  & =Φ(1.44)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.44)≈0.9251.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W<653) & ≈Φ(1.44) \\  & ≈0.9251.\end{aligned}
$$
